chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of his companions, from Ja'far ibn Anbasa, from Ubada ibn Ziyad Al-Asadi, from Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and Ahmad ibn Muhammad Al-Asimi, from the one who narrated to him, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) wrote in his letter to Al- Hasan (peace be upon him): 'Beware of excessive vigilance (ghayra) in places where it is not due, for that calls the sound/healthy one among them to illness. But regulate their affairs; if you see a flaw, hasten to express disapproval regarding both the small and the large. And if you discern doubt/suspicion from them, then the sin becomes great and the reprimand becomes light.'

key_terms.السَّقَمِ: Illness (metaphorical for moral or spiritual decline)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper balance of vigilance (ghayra) in managing family affairs according to Imam Ali's letter?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the nuanced Shia understanding of *al-ghayra* (protective jealousy) as a balanced virtue rather than excessive suspicion, warning that misplaced vigilance can induce 'illness' in the healthy. It provides practical guidance for family governance, instructing the head of the household to promptly address minor faults in both wives and children to prevent the escalation of doubt (*rayb*) and the magnification of sin. This reflects the Imams' emphasis on emotional intelligence and measured discipline within the domestic sphere.
